unit_description: This unit introduces fractions by partitioning shapes into equal parts. Students identify equal and unequal parts, make halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, and eighths, and name unit fractions.
unit_goals: Identify equal and unequal parts of shapes.
Name unit fractions of partitioned shapes.
Understand that equal parts are the same size.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students learn to partition shapes into equal parts and name unit fractions.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by folding or drawing lines to split shapes.
lessons.concept: A fraction is made when a whole is split into equal parts. Equal parts are the same size. Unequal parts are different sizes and do not make fractions.
lessons.practice: Identify whether shapes are split into equal or unequal parts.
lessons.objective: Identify equal and unequal parts of shapes.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by checking for equal parts.

questions.prompt: A circle is split into two parts that are the same size. Are they equal?
A rectangle is split into three parts of different sizes. Are they equal?
To name a fraction, must the parts be equal?

learn.title: Identify Equal and Unequal Parts
teaching_points: Equal parts are the same size and shape.
If parts are not equal, you cannot name them with a fraction.

example.prompt: Which shape is divided into equal parts?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A square is split into 4 parts. Two parts are large and two are small. Are the parts equal?
try_it.hint: All parts must be the same size.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Tell whether each shape is divided into equal or unequal parts.

flashcards.title: Equal Parts Vocabulary
flashcards.instructions: Review equal and unequal parts vocabulary.

bigIdea.title: Identify Equal and Unequal Parts
bigIdea.subtitle: Fractions need equal parts
bigIdea.intro: Before you can name a fraction, the whole must be split into equal parts. Equal parts are exactly the same size.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why must parts be equal to name a fraction?

ruleCards.description: Equal parts can be named with fractions.
Unequal parts cannot be named with fractions.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by partitioning shapes into 2, 3, and 4 equal parts.
lessons.concept: Partitioning means splitting a whole into equal parts. Halves are 2 equal parts, thirds are 3 equal parts, and fourths are 4 equal parts.
lessons.practice: Partition shapes into halves, thirds, and fourths and name each part.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with halves, thirds, and fourths.

questions.prompt: How many equal parts are in halves?
How many equal parts are in thirds?
How many equal parts are in fourths?

example.prompt: Show a rectangle divided into fourths.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Divide a circle into 3 equal parts. What fraction is one part?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Partition each shape into the given number of equal parts and name one part.

bigIdea.title: Make Halves, Thirds, and Fourths
bigIdea.subtitle: Partition into equal parts
bigIdea.intro: When you split a whole into 2, 3, or 4 equal parts, you have halves, thirds, or fourths. Each part is named with a unit fraction.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do you make equal parts look the same?

ruleCards.description: Each part is one of two equal parts.
Each part is one of four equal parts.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by partitioning shapes into 6 and 8 equal parts.
lessons.concept: A whole can be split into more equal parts. Sixths are 6 equal parts and eighths are 8 equal parts. The more parts, the smaller each part is.
lessons.practice: Partition shapes into sixths and eighths and name each part.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with sixths and eighths.

questions.prompt: How many equal parts are in sixths?
How many equal parts are in eighths?
Which is smaller: 1/6 or 1/8 of the same whole?

learn.title: Make Sixths and Eighths
teaching_points: More parts means each part is smaller.

example.prompt: Show a rectangle divided into eighths.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Divide a circle into 6 equal parts. What fraction is one part?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Partition each shape into sixths or eighths and name one part.

bigIdea.title: Make Sixths and Eighths
bigIdea.subtitle: More parts, smaller pieces
bigIdea.intro: As you split a whole into more equal parts, each part gets smaller. Sixths are smaller than fourths, and eighths are smaller than sixths.

ruleCards.description: Each part is one of six equal parts.
Each part is smaller because the whole is split into more pieces.

lessons.lesson_title: Name Unit Fractions of Partitioned Shapes
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by naming one part of shapes divided into 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 parts.
lessons.concept: A unit fraction names one equal part of a whole. It has 1 on top and the total number of equal parts on the bottom. One of four equal parts is 1/4.
lessons.practice: Name unit fractions for partitioned shapes.
lessons.objective: Name unit fractions of partitioned shapes.

questions.prompt: One part of a shape divided into 4 equal parts is what fraction?
One part of a shape divided into 8 equal parts is what fraction?
What is the name for one of three equal parts?

learn.title: Name Unit Fractions of Partitioned Shapes
teaching_points: A unit fraction has 1 as the numerator.
The denominator is the total number of equal parts.
Count the equal parts to write the fraction.

example.prompt: A circle is divided into 5 equal parts. What fraction is one part?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 6 equal parts. What fraction is one part?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Name the unit fraction for one shaded part of each shape.

bigIdea.title: Name Unit Fractions of Partitioned Shapes
bigIdea.subtitle: One part of the whole
bigIdea.intro: A unit fraction tells about one equal part. The bottom number tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. The top number is always 1 for a unit fraction.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What does the bottom number of a unit fraction tell you?

ruleCards.description: The numerator is 1 because it is one part.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole.

lessons.lesson_title: Unit Evaluation: Equal Parts and Unit Fractions
lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of equal and unequal parts, halves/thirds/fourths, sixths/eighths, and naming unit fractions.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: equal and unequal parts, halves/thirds/fourths, sixths/eighths, and naming unit fractions.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about equal parts and unit fractions.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: A shape is split into 5 equal parts. What fraction is one part?
A circle is split into two parts of different sizes. Can you name a fraction?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: equal/unequal + halves/thirds/fourths + sixths/eighths + unit fractions = equal parts and unit fractions

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 4 equal parts. What fraction is one part?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 26 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 26 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Equal Parts and Unit Fractions
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: equal and unequal parts, halves/thirds/fourths, sixths/eighths, and naming unit fractions.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about equal parts and unit fractions?

ruleCards.description: Fractions only work when parts are equal.
The numerator is 1; the denominator is the number of equal parts.
